code: library(geokit)

previous_headings: Search and Filter Single-Cell Studies of Urothelial Carcinoma
what: 1. Search for Related Series by Keywords (e.g., Bladder/Urothelial Cancer)
title: Build Your Own GEOmetadb
text: Based NCBI Eutils query, details can found : Querying GEO DataSets
code: uc_gse <- list(     geo_search(         "bladder cancer[ALL] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND GSE[ETYP]"     ),     geo_search(         "urothelial cancer[ALL] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND GSE[ETYP]"     ) ) #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  664/663 [322/s] | ETA:  0s #> → Parsing GEO records #> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  664/663 [322/s] | ETA:  0sGet records from NCBI for 663 queries in 2.1s #>  #> → Parsing GEO records uc_gse <- unique(dplyr::bind_rows(uc_gse))

previous_headings: Search and Filter Single-Cell Studies of Urothelial Carcinoma
what: 2. Extract Sample Count from the “Contains” Field
title: Build Your Own GEOmetadb
code: uc_gse$number_of_samples <- stringr::str_match(   uc_gse$Contains, "(\\d+) Samples?" )[, 2L, drop = TRUE]  # Quick Statistics max_samples <- max(as.numeric(uc_gse$number_of_samples), na.rm = TRUE) median_samples <- median(as.numeric(uc_gse$number_of_samples), na.rm = TRUE) top_series <- dplyr::slice_max(uc_gse, as.numeric(number_of_samples))

previous_headings: Search and Filter Single-Cell Studies of Urothelial Carcinoma
what: 3. Fetch Series Metadata (Parallel Processing and Batch Saving to Local Directory)
title: Build Your Own GEOmetadb
code: uc_gse_meta <- geo_meta(uc_gse[["Series Accession"]],   odir = "gse_urothelial_cancer" )

what: 4. Filter Possible Single-Cell Studies (Search for Keywords in Summary/Title/Design)
title: Build Your Own GEOmetadb
text: following steps, successfully created GEOmetadb!
code: uc_gse_sc <- dplyr::filter(   uc_gse_meta,   dplyr::if_any(     c(Series_summary, Series_title, Series_overall_design),     grepl,     pattern = "single[- ]cell|scRNA", ignore.case = TRUE   ) ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     number_of_samples = lengths(       strsplit(Series_sample_id, "; ", fixed = TRUE)     )   )  # Output Results and Statistics dplyr::slice_max(uc_gse_sc, number_of_samples)$Series_geo_accession max(uc_gse_sc$number_of_samples, na.rm = TRUE) median(uc_gse_sc$number_of_samples, na.rm = TRUE) writexl::write_xlsx(uc_gse_sc, "uc_gse_sc.xlsx")

title: Virtual class for holding GEO series, samples, platforms, and datasets. — GEOSoft-class
text: metadata: list, containing header metadata informations. rcd_type character indicating type record (e.g., Platform, Sample, Series, Datasets). rcd_name character representing name associated record (e.g., GEO dataset name). usually matches accession, may differ cases. accession: character giving geo accession id current GEO series, samples, platforms, datasets. columns: data.frame gives datatable header descriptions. rownmaes data.frame column names slot datatable. datatable: data.frame shows data information. gsm: list GEOSoft object containg samples information current GEO platform. gse: list GEOSoft object containg series information current GEO platform. gpl: list GEOSoft object containg platforms information current GEO series.

title: GEO accession type — geo_gtype
text: Determine type GEO accession ID (e.g. DataSet, Series, Sample, Platform). function inspects accession prefix returns corresponding GEO type, optionally abbreviated form.

title: GEO accession type — geo_gtype
code: geo_gtype(accession, abbre = FALSE)

title: GEO accession type — geo_gtype
text: accession character GEO accession IDs. Examples: DataSets (GDS): "GDS505", "GDS606", "GDS1234", "GDS9999", etc. Series (GSE): "GSE2", "GSE22", "GSE100", "GSE2000", etc. Platforms (GPL): "GPL96", "GPL570", "GPL10558", etc. Samples (GSM): "GSM12345", "GSM67890", "GSM112233", etc. abbre logical scalar indicating whether abbreviate GEO type return value. FALSE (default), full type name returned; TRUE, short abbreviation used.

title: GEO accession type — geo_gtype
text: character GEO accession type.

title: GEO accession type — geo_gtype
code: geo_gtype("GSE10") #> [1] "Series" geo_gtype("gpl98") #> [1] "Platforms" geo_gtype("GSM1") #> [1] "Samples" geo_gtype("GDS10") #> [1] "Datasets"  # use abbreviation geo_gtype("GSE10", TRUE) #> [1] "GSE" geo_gtype("gpl98", TRUE) #> [1] "GPL" geo_gtype("GSM1", TRUE) #> [1] "GSM" geo_gtype("GDS10", TRUE) #> [1] "GDS"

title: Retrieve Series Matrix and Create ExpressionSet — geo_matrix
text: accession character GEO accession IDs. Examples: DataSets (GDS): "GDS505", "GDS606", "GDS1234", "GDS9999", etc. Series (GSE): "GSE2", "GSE22", "GSE100", "GSE2000", etc. Platforms (GPL): "GPL96", "GPL570", "GPL10558", etc. Samples (GSM): "GSM12345", "GSM67890", "GSM112233", etc. add_gpl Logical NULL. Whether include platform information (featureData slot). NULL (default), function attempts map GPL accession Bioconductor annotation package. successful, annotation slot updated add_gpl set FALSE; otherwise, add_gpl set TRUE. pdata_from_soft Logical. Specifies whether derive phenoData GSE series SOFT file. Defaults FALSE, case phenoData parsed directly series matrix file. Set TRUE encounter issues parsing characteristics_ch* columns correctly, attempt retrieve data SOFT file instead. ftp_over_https Logical scalar. TRUE, connects GEO FTP server via HTTPS (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo); otherwise uses plain FTP (ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo). applicable GEO FTP server access. handle_opts list named options / headers set multi_download. odir Destination directory downloads. Defaults current working directory.

what: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
text: Create QueryChat object exploring GEO metadata LLM. Use geo_qc() create chat object, geo_shiny() launch Shiny app, geo_chat() start console chat.

title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
code: geo_qc(client, data_source, table_name = NULL, ..., instructions = NULL)  geo_shiny(...)  geo_chat(...)

title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
text: client Optional chat client. Can : ellmer::Chat object string pass ellmer::chat() (e.g., "openai/gpt-4o") NULL (default): Uses querychat.client option, QUERYCHAT_CLIENT environment variable, defaults ellmer::chat_openai() data_source data.frame database connection containing GEO metadata, typically geo_meta() geo_search(). table_name string specifying table name use SQL queries. data_source data.frame, name refer queries (typically variable name). provided, inferred variable name data.frame inputs. database connections, parameter required. ... Arguments passed querychat::querychat id Optional module ID QueryChat instance. provided, auto-generated table_name. ID used namespace Shiny module. greeting Optional initial message display users. Can character string (Markdown format) file path. provided, greeting generated start conversation using LLM, adds latency cost. Use $generate_greeting() create greeting save reuse. tools querychat tools include chat client, default. "update" includes tools updating resetting dashboard "query" includes tool executing SQL queries. Use tools = "update" want dashboard updating tools, want disable querying tool entirely prevent LLM seeing data dataset. data_description Optional description data plain text Markdown. Can string file path. provides context LLM data represents. categorical_threshold text columns, maximum number unique values consider categorical variable. Default 20. cleanup Whether automatically run $cleanup() Shiny session/app stops. default, cleanup occurs QueryChat created within Shiny app. Set TRUE always clean , FALSE never clean automatically. querychat_app(), -memory databases created data frames always cleaned . bookmark_store bookmarking storage method. Passed shiny::enableBookmarking(). "url" "server", chat state (including current query) bookmarked. Default "url". instructions Optional single string additional instructions append default GEO metadata assistant instructions.

title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
text: QueryChat object configured data_source, LLM client, GEO-specific instructions.

title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
text: geo_qc() intentionally serialize rows build large data prompt. Instead, delegates schema summarization, SQL querying, dashboard filtering QueryChat. three exported helpers differ far take QueryChat workflow: geo_qc() creates returns QueryChat object. Use want inspect generated prompt, customize object, embed another Shiny app, launch app/console later qc$app() qc$console(). geo_shiny() creates QueryChat object immediately launches Shiny app. Use interactive browser-based filtering exploration. geo_chat() creates QueryChat object immediately starts console chat. Use command-line exploration without opening Shiny app. default instructions guide assistant query filter GEO metadata, identify relevant studies, generate reproducible R code asked, preserve explicit accession IDs, explain GEO accession types (GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS) useful. first argument LLM client. Use client = NULL pass NULL first positional argument let querychat choose client options environment variables. Additional context data_description, greeting, tools, categorical_threshold, cleanup can passed ... querychat::querychat(). prompt_template intentionally forwarded geo_qc() supplies GEO-specific instructions extra_instructions.

title: Chat with GEO metadata using natural language — geo_qc
code: if (requireNamespace("querychat", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE)) {     records <- data.frame(         Accession = c("GSE1", "GSE2"),         Title = c("human diabetes study", "mouse liver study"),         Type = c("Expression profiling by array", "RNA-seq"),         Samples = c(12L, 8L)     )     qc <- geo_qc(NULL, records, table_name = "geo_records", cleanup = TRUE)     qc$cleanup() }

title: Search GEO database — geo_search
text: Search GDS database return search results data frame.

title: Search GEO database — geo_search
code: geo_search(query, step = 500L, interval = NULL)

title: Search GEO database — geo_search
text: query character string search term. NCBI uses fielded search syntax. example, "Homo sapiens[ORGN]" searches "Organism" field Homo sapiens. See GEO query tutorial details. Searchable fields can listed rentrez::entrez_db_searchable("gds"). step Integer. Number records fetch per request. Use smaller value requests fail. interval Numeric. Time interval (seconds) successive requests. Defaults 0. Increase value requests fail due rate limits.

title: Search GEO database — geo_search
text: data frame contains search results

title: Search GEO database — geo_search
text: NCBI allows higher request limits (10 per second) using API key. can set key current R session rentrez::set_entrez_key(), permanently setting ENTREZ_KEY environment variable via Sys.setenv(). set, rentrez automatically use key NCBI requests. See rentrez tutorial details.

The study aimed to elucidate how glucose levels and endothelial interaction influence pericyte gene expression, providing insights into the cellular mechanisms potentially involved in diabetic retinopathy. #> 2  Atherosclerosis drives cardiovascular morbidity in diabetes, with endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) as a key contributor. While epigenetic regulators are increasingly implicated in atherosclerotic progression, the specific role of Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone methyltransferase, in EndMT in diabetes-associated atherosclerosis remains unclear. We show that EZH2-mediated H3K27 trimethylation is elevated in carotid plaques from diabetic patients and in aortic endothelium of diabetic Apoe-/- mice. more... #> 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      We performed transcriptomics analysis on the placental tissues from gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) patients and normal pregnant participants. #> 4 Obesity is a known risk factor for diseases of the pancreas, including diabetes, pancreatic cancer and pancreatitis, but mechanisms remain unclear. To elucidate how obesity impacts pancreatic immune homeostasis, we performed spatial, transcriptomic and functional profiling of human pancreatic immune cells from obese and non-obese organ donors. title: Retrieve GEO SOFT file from NCBI GEO — geo_soft
text: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) NCBI serves public repository wide range high-throughput experimental data. data include single dual channel microarray-based experiments measuring mRNA, genomic DNA, protein abundance, well non-array techniques serial analysis gene expression (SAGE), mass spectrometry proteomic data. basic level organization GEO, three entity types may supplied users: Platforms, Samples, Series. Additionally, curated entity called GEO dataset. Platform record describes list elements array (e.g., cDNAs, oligonucleotide probesets, ORFs, antibodies) list elements may detected quantified experiment (e.g., SAGE tags, peptides). Platform record assigned unique stable GEO accession number (GPLxxx). Platform may reference many Samples/Series submitted multiple submitters. Sample record describes conditions individual Sample handled, manipulations underwent, abundance measurement element derived . Sample record assigned unique stable GEO accession number (GSMxxx). Sample entity must reference one Platform may included multiple Series. Series record defines set related Samples considered part group, Samples related, ordered. Series provides focal point description experiment whole. Series records may also contain tables describing extracted data, summary conclusions, analyses. Series record assigned unique stable GEO accession number (GSExxx). GEO DataSets (GDSxxx) curated sets GEO Sample data. GDS record represents collection biologically statistically comparable GEO Samples forms basis GEO's suite data display analysis tools. Samples within GDS refer Platform, , share common set probe elements. Value measurements Sample within GDS assumed calculated equivalent manner, , considerations background processing normalization consistent across dataset. Information reflecting experimental design provided GDS subsets.

title: GEO URL resolver — geo_url

title: GEO URL resolver — geo_url
text: accession character GEO accession IDs. Examples: DataSets (GDS): "GDS505", "GDS606", "GDS1234", "GDS9999", etc. Series (GSE): "GSE2", "GSE22", "GSE100", "GSE2000", etc. Platforms (GPL): "GPL96", "GPL570", "GPL10558", etc. Samples (GSM): "GSM12345", "GSM67890", "GSM112233", etc. format character specifying file format type requested. GEO data can accessed two sites: Direct FTP/HTTPS file retrieval GEO FTP server (file type): "soft": SOFT (Simple Omnibus Text Format) GEO FTP site. accession DataSets Series, default. "soft_full": full SOFT (Simple Omnibus Text Format) files GEO FTP site DataSet (GDS) containging additionally contains --date gene annotation DataSet Platform. "miniml": MINiML (MIAME Notation Markup Language, pronounced miniml) XML format incorporates experimental data metadata. MINiML essentially XML rendering SOFT format. "matrix": Series matrix file. "annot": annotation files Platforms. "suppl": supplementary files. file retrieval Accession Display Bar GEO database: "text": machine-readable SOFT format (Simple Omnibus Format Text). "xml": XML format. "html": human-readable format hyperlinks (downloadable entry available). following table summarizes compatibility GEO accession types file format options: amount character specifying amount data (applicable Accession Display Bar access): "none": Applicable DataSets; DataSets, also sole valid option. "brief": accession attributes . "quick": accession attributes + first 20 rows data table. "data": omits accession's attributes, showing links accessions full data table. "full": accession attributes + complete data table. scope character specifying GEO accessions include (applicable Accession Display Bar access). "none": Applicable DataSets; DataSets, also sole valid option "self": queried accession . "gsm", "gpl", "gse": related samples, platforms, series. "": accessions related query (family view). ftp_over_https Logical scalar. TRUE, connects GEO FTP server via HTTPS (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo); otherwise uses plain FTP (ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo). applicable GEO FTP server access.
